task: EPMCDME-14072 — Added an optional nested camelCase `oauth` block (ManagedMcpOAuthConfig) to the ManagedMcpServer catalog model so GET /v1/mcp/managed-servers publishes self-describing, secret-free per-server OAuth client parameters, backward compatible with entries that omit it.

component_scope.label: S
component_scope.affected: ManagedMcpOAuthConfig (new nested pydantic model), ManagedMcpServer catalog model, _use_default_if_none BeforeValidator, managed-mcp-servers.example.yaml schema documentation
component_scope.layers: Config/Model (catalog loader), API response contract (no router code change), Deployment config (ConfigMap example)

requirements_clarity.label: S
requirements_clarity.gaps: One edge-case semantic was unspecified and surfaced only during code review (CR-001): whether a blank `callbackHost:` YAML key (parses as None, not as an absent key) should fall back to the documented default or invalidate the entry. Field list, defaults, port range and camelCase-only spelling were otherwise fully specified up front.

technical_risk.label: M
technical_risk.risk_factors: Publishes OAuth client configuration (clientId, scope, loopback callback, IdP authorize/token URLs) to external agent clients — the secret-free contract must hold, since the catalog is served as-is; fail-closed validation means one malformed `oauth` key drops the entire server entry from the catalog; pydantic v2 defaults do not absorb an explicit None, a non-obvious behaviour that produced a real defect
technical_risk.mitigation: Additive optional field, fully backward compatible; deprecated scalar `auth` retained and never derived from `oauth`; per-entry validation failures are logged and degrade to skipping one entry rather than raising; `extra="ignore"` allows ConfigMap to run ahead of a backend rollout; blank-key defect fixed with a BeforeValidator raising PydanticUseDefault so the default stays defined once on the Field; 9 added tests cover defaults, blank keys, missing required keys, out-of-range port, snake_case rejection and camelCase wire format; trivially reversible (no persisted state)

affected_layers.label: S
layers_changed: Config/Model (managed MCP catalog loader and models)
API response contract (schema only — router unchanged, response_model_by_alias defaults to True)
Deployment config (customer ConfigMap catalog schema, documented via example YAML)

key_reasoning.reason: Base risk was S — a purely additive optional pydantic field on an existing loader that already had a graceful-degradation contract, with no persisted state and trivial rollback. Bumped to M by the authorization red flag: the published block is OAuth client configuration consumed by external agent clients, so the secret-free invariant is load-bearing, and fail-closed validation means an operator typo silently removes a whole server from the catalog. The pydantic-v2 None-vs-absent defect (CR-001) confirms the non-zero risk was real rather than theoretical.

4 files changed, 325 insertions / 7 deletions, zero new files — every touched file already existed. Two of the four are tests (13 to 22 tests on the affected files), so production surface is a single module plus its example-YAML documentation. Bottom of the M band per the actual-mode file-count mapping; by the guide's modified/new split (4 modified, 0 new) it would read as S.

One component: a new nested model inside the existing ManagedMcpServer catalog model, matching the guide's S archetype 'add a new field to an existing endpoint response'. No layer boundary was crossed — the router needed no change because FastAPI serializes by alias by default, and no service, repository, DB or external call was touched.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped from S (2) to M (3): change affects authorization configuration — the endpoint now publishes per-server OAuth client parameters (clientId, scope, authorize/token URLs) consumed by external agent clients, making the secret-free contract and fail-closed entry validation security-relevant.
